https://www.digitalspy.com/tv/a73317116/.text: Jared Leto promised on stage to sign women’s breasts at a 30 Seconds to Mars aftershow party the first time I saw him perform in London in 2009. At the time the comment was innocuous. That’s just what rock stars say.But now it feels all the more chilling after one of the women who came forward in BBC documentary Jared Leto: Hollywood’s Dark Secret insisted that when she was 14, he instructed a security guard to take her backstage at a music festival after having made a lewd comment about her chest during an autograph-signing. The girl's mother confronted Leto, but he repeated the comment, it is alleged.The woman is one of 10 who have come forward with allegations of sexual assault, grooming and statutory rape all taking place between 2002 and 2016, when he was in his 30s and 40s. He is now 54. Leto vehemently denies all the allegations. Hours after the documentary was released, a spokesperson for Leto issued a statement on his behalf, saying: "I have never sexually assaulted anyone in my entire life. These claims are absolutely and categorically false."I met Leto in the middle of that time, six months after I’d watched him perform on stage with his band at Koko, London.At the time he was marketed as a sex symbol who couldn’t get enough female attention. Women were literally throwing their knickers at him.But now as revelations emerge, I can reveal that what he was marketed as may have fuelled his alleged predatory behaviour and that Leto was actually a man wracked by low self esteem, overwhelm and stress.Six months after that gig at Koko, London in November 2009, I flew to Sziget Festival in Budapest in August 2010 where Leto’s band was also on the bill.I was working for the Daily Star’s music column Playlist at the time and had an interview with Mika lined up. But when Mika and I were talking backstage, Leto emerged stressed and frantic following his headline slot at the festival.After performing to thousands of fans, the then-38-year-old unleashed his performance anxieties, saying: "I'm not sure how good that performance was. I don't know if I sang enough – I should have sung more and danced less."His eyes were frantic. I had never seen a pop star so worried about their image.Mika and I tried to appease him. But Leto seemed on the verge of tears reflecting on his crippling jet lag and late nights.He said: "I feel so tired all the time, it's really exhausting and never ending."Leto’s insecurities felt like such a different persona from the confident, sex symbol one the public were being sold. He wasn’t sexy. He seemed desperate to be liked and loved.With so many women speaking out against him, I now fear that these insecurities mixed with an over-the-top sex symbol status he needed to maintain seeped its way into his alleged despicable treatment of women and that perhaps – like so often does with predatory, toxic men – these women became victims as his life spiralled out of control.Jared Leto: Hollywood's Dark Secret is streaming on BBC iPlayer.If you've been affected by the issues raised in this story, you can access more information from Rape Crisis England and Wales, which works towards the elimination of all forms of sexual violence and sexual misconduct, on its website or by calling the National Rape Crisis Helpline on 0808 802 9999. Rape Crisis Scotland's helpline number is 08088 01 03 02.Readers in the US are encouraged to contact RAINN, or the National Sexual Assault Hotline on 800-656-4673.

https://www.ksl.com:443/article/news/wor.text: Russia pounds Kyiv, kills 10 as Ukraine appeals for Patriot interceptors     KEY TAKEAWAYS Russia's missile attack on Kyiv killed 10 people, damaging infrastructure and homes. Ukraine's President Zelensky urges for more Patriot interceptors amid depleted supplies. Kyiv's Mayor Klitschko prepares shelters as Foreign Minister Sybiha requests air defense aid. KYIV — Russia pounded Kyiv and the region in a heavy ballistic missile attack early on Saturday, killing 10 people, as President Volodymyr ​Zelensky warned that Ukraine had run out of interceptor missiles for its U.S. Patriot air defence systems. Zelensky said that Russia launched 35 missiles at Ukraine, including 27 ballistic missiles, and also 185 drones. Only one ballistic missile was intercepted, "simply because there are ‌no interceptors for the Patriot system", he said. More than a dozen explosions reverberated through the city during several waves of attacks, according to Reuters witnesses. "Every package of ballistic missile interceptors saves ⁠the lives of our people. And every night without them results ​in more casualties," Zelensky said on the Telegram app. With the war ⁠in its fifth year, fighting is raging along about 1,200 kilometres (750 miles) of front line. But Russian advances have slowed by more than half ‌this year, and Ukraine has been ‌launching strikes inside Russia, hitting its oil facilities, logistics sites and weapons production. Ukraine was bringing back war to Russia, ⁠Zelensky said, adding that his troops struck the infrastructure of three oil refineries in the ⁠Bashkortostan region and other targets that sustained Moscow's war effort. Russia has also intensified its attacks on Kyiv and other Ukrainian cities. Ukraine relies on U.S.-made Patriot air defence systems, but the Iran war has seen supplies of interceptor missiles previously earmarked for Ukraine diverted to the U.S. military and U.S. allies in the Gulf. Moscow and Kyiv both deny targeting civilians in the war launched by Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine in February 2022. Second major attack on Kyiv this week Saturday's is the second major attack on Kyiv this week after ‌nine people, including six members of one family in a village near Kryvyi Rih, were killed ​on Thursday and a suspected Russian cruise missile landed in Poland. Damage was recorded in seven districts across Kyiv, a city of about 3 million people, the Prosecutor's General Office said after Saturday's attacks. Zelensky said that fires broke out across Kyiv and 18 residential buildings, a school, the Lithuanian Embassy, and infrastructure facilities were damaged. Ukrainian prosecutors said seven people were killed in the Darnytskyi district on the left bank of the Dnipro river and two more people died in the Solomyanskyi district on the right bank of the city. One more person was killed in the Kyiv region, where the attacks damaged several warehouses, regional officials said. Dozens of people in Kyiv and the region ​were injured, including four children who suffered multiple shrapnel wounds and lacerations. "I looked at my phone; it was 1:30 (22:30 GMT) and sirens (blared). I was lying dressed in my bed; I got up ‌immediately. And at once explosions ⁠started — boom, boom," said Nadiia Komarova, a 68-year-old concierge at an apartment building in Kyiv. "Our ceilings have started to crumble. My window here is smashed, and everything has fallen inside," she told Reuters. Reuters television footage showed police and rescuers working on the site. Two rescuers put a body in a black sack in a car. Firefighters were extinguishing fires and charred cars stood near an apartment building. Mayor Vitali Klitschko said Kyiv was working to ‌build and prepare more shelters as attacks ​continue to intensify. Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha issued a fresh plea for urgent air defence ‌supplies: "It is the battle for the ⁠skies that will define the ​trajectory of this war. The stronger the air shield over Ukraine, the closer peace becomes." × Photos The Key Takeaways for this article were generated with the assistance of large language models and reviewed by our editorial team. https://hotnews.ro/zelenski-spune-ca-res.text: Președintele ucrainean Volodimir Zelenski a declarat vineri că restricțiile de viteză impuse sistemului american Starshield, versiunea militară a serviciului de internet prin satelit Starlink al SpaceX, sunt în continuare în vigoare, afectând capacitatea armatei ucrainene de a desfășura operațiuni pe teritoriul țării, potrivit Reuters. „Din păcate, restricțiile de viteză se mențin de-a lungul întregii linii a frontului și în teritoriile Ucrainei ocupate temporar”, a spus Zelenski în mesajul său video transmis vineri seară. „Mă aștept ca Ministerul Apărării și Ministerul de Externe, împreună cu toate structurile relevante din Statele Unite, să găsească o soluție la această problemă”, a adăugat liderul ucrainean. Zelenski anunțase joi că restricțiile de viteză impuse serviciului Starshield au fost reintroduse. Liderul de la Kiev a declarat că restricțiile au afectat, timp de mai multe zile, operațiunile militare ucrainene de-a lungul întregii linii a frontului și în teritoriile ocupate de Rusia. El a mai spus că armata ucraineană a investigat perturbările și a ajuns la concluzia că nu este vorba despre erori tehnice întâmplătoare, ci despre restricții sistematice. „Pentru noi, acest lucru înseamnă, înainte de toate, o îngreunare semnificativă a interceptării dronelor rusești propulsate cu reacție”, a declarat Zelenski. „Din păcate, au avut deja loc atacuri care au reușit să își atingă țintele, deoarece sistemele noastre de interceptare nu pot atinge viteze suficient de mari și nu reușesc să intercepteze dronele la timp”, a mai transmis acesta. Zelenski a avertizat că restricțiile ajută Rusia să desfășoare atacuri mai precise și provoacă noi pierderi de vieți omenești în rândul ucrainenilor.
